editorial:
When Ann, George, and their young son Georgie pull up to their lakeside vacation home, everything feels calm and normal. That peace shatters when two polite young men named Peter and Paul show up asking to borrow eggs. What starts as a small favor turns into a nightmare as the pair trap the family inside their own house. The vibe is tense and uncomfortable from the start, with the boys acting friendly while clearly enjoying the power they hold. You feel the dread building slowly, and the movie never lets you look away.

The acting is strong across the board, especially from Naomi Watts and Tim Roth as the terrified parents. Michael Pitt is chilling as the smug leader of the two intruders. The pacing is slow and deliberate, which works for some viewers but may frustrate others looking for fast action. The movie also breaks the fourth wall, which is either clever or annoying depending on your taste. If you enjoy dark thrillers that challenge you, this is worth a look. Stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, George and Georgie are both killed by Peter and Paul. Ann is taken out on a boat, where Paul asks if she wants to bet on her survival. When she briefly escapes, Paul literally rewinds the movie to undo her attempt, then shoots her. The killers simply move on to the next house, starting the cycle again. There is no rescue and no happy ending, just a cold reminder that the violence continues.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves dark thrillers and psychological horror.
